angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 8,247,927 km at 68.47 pc = 1.61 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 14.6042 +/- 0.1028 mas (same row, RUWE 1.00): 68.47 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 11.856 (11.607 to 12.105) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source): 8,247,927 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 2.703 (2.500 to 3.005) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4666 +/- 0.6 K from Andrae et al. (2023), A&A 674, A27 (Gaia DR3 GSP-Phot), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 398030875774246656: teff_gspphot 4665.719 K (16th-84th percentiles 4665.1074-4666.3804), the temperature FLAME used (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202243462). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Andrae et al. (2023), A&A 674, A27 (Gaia DR3 GSP-Phot), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 398030875774246656: teff_gspphot 4665.719 K (16th-84th percentiles 4665.1074-4666.3804), the temperature FLAME used (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202243462)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/adhil.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 2.722, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
